title: CTS The Doctrine of Man — Unit 5

blocks.en: 📖 Systematic Theology — Unit 5: The Doctrine of Man
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Teología Sistemática — Unidad 5: La Doctrina del Hombre

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "What is man that You are mindful of him?" — Psalm 8:4 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "¿Qué es el hombre, para que tengas de él memoria?" — Salmo 8:4 (RVG)

blocks.en: Day 1 — What Is Man? The Central Question
blocks.es_reference: Día 1 — ¿Qué es el Hombre? La Pregunta Central

blocks.en: To understand theology correctly, one must eventually ask a simple but profound question: What is man?
blocks.es_reference: Para entender correctamente la teología, uno debe eventualmente preguntar una pregunta simple pero profunda: ¿Qué es el hombre?

blocks.en: This question cannot be avoided. Every worldview attempts to answer it. Some say man is nothing more than a biological organism shaped by evolution and environment. Others define him by culture, experience, or personal identity. Still others assume that man is essentially good and only needs improvement.
blocks.es_reference: Esta pregunta no puede evitarse. Cada cosmovisión intenta responderla. Algunos dicen que el hombre no es más que un organismo biológico moldeado por la evolución y el medio ambiente. Otros lo definen por la cultura, la experiencia o la identidad personal. Otros asumen que el hombre es esencialmente bueno y solo necesita mejora.

blocks.en: Scripture presents a very different picture. Man is not self-defined or self-created, nor is he independent. He is a created being, and his identity can only be understood in relation to the One who made him.
blocks.es_reference: La Escritura presenta una imagen muy diferente. El hombre no es autodefinido ni autocreado, ni es independiente. Es un ser creado, y su identidad solo puede entenderse en relación con Aquel que lo hizo.

blocks.en: The Bible begins with God, not man. This is not accidental. Until we understand God, we will never understand ourselves. The moment man attempts to define himself apart from God, he loses both his identity and his purpose.
blocks.es_reference: La Biblia comienza con Dios, no con el hombre. Esto no es accidental. Hasta que entendamos a Dios, nunca nos entenderemos a nosotros mismos. En el momento en que el hombre intenta definirse aparte de Dios, pierde tanto su identidad como su propósito.

blocks.en: Man is created, accountable, and dependent. He does not originate himself, he does not sustain himself, and he is not the final authority over himself. Man is not only created by God—he is created for God.
blocks.es_reference: El hombre es creado, responsable y dependiente. No se origina a sí mismo, no se sostiene a sí mismo y no es la autoridad final sobre sí mismo. El hombre no solo es creado por Dios—es creado para Dios.

blocks.en: Man is also a unity of body and soul, not a soul that merely happens to carry a body. The body is not a prison or an afterthought but part of what God made and called good. The clearest confirmation of this is the Incarnation: when the Son of God took on real human flesh and lived within genuine human limits, He honored the body by assuming one, and His bodily resurrection shows that God’s purpose is to redeem the body, not to discard it. So to be human is to be an embodied person, and what affects the body affects the whole self.
blocks.es_reference: El hombre es también una unidad de cuerpo y alma, no un alma que simplemente lleva un cuerpo. El cuerpo no es una prisión ni algo secundario, sino parte de lo que Dios hizo y llamó bueno. La confirmación más clara de esto es la Encarnación: cuando el Hijo de Dios tomó verdadera carne humana y vivió dentro de límites humanos genuinos, honró el cuerpo al asumir uno, y Su resurrección corporal muestra que el propósito de Dios es redimir el cuerpo, no desecharlo. Así que ser humano es ser una persona encarnada, y lo que afecta al cuerpo afecta a todo el ser.

blocks.en: Human dignity and human responsibility are inseparable. Man has value because he is created by God, and he has responsibility because he lives under God.
blocks.es_reference: La dignidad humana y la responsabilidad humana son inseparables. El hombre tiene valor porque es creado por Dios, y tiene responsabilidad porque vive bajo Dios.

blocks.en: If we misunderstand man at this point, everything else in theology begins to unravel. Sin will be misunderstood. Salvation will be misunderstood. Even the gospel itself will be distorted. The doctrine of man is not secondary. It is foundational.
blocks.es_reference: Si malinterpretamos al hombre en este punto, todo lo demás en la teología comienza a desmoronarse. El pecado será malinterpretado. La salvación será malinterpretada. Incluso el evangelio mismo se distorsionará. La doctrina del hombre no es secundaria. Es fundamental.

blocks.en: Day 2 — Created in the Image of God
blocks.es_reference: Día 2 — Creado a Imagen de Dios

blocks.en: The foundational truth of human existence is that man is created in the image of God.
blocks.es_reference: La verdad fundamental de la existencia humana es que el hombre es creado a imagen de Dios.

blocks.en: "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness." — Genesis 1:26
blocks.es_reference: "Hagamos al hombre a nuestra imagen, conforme a nuestra semejanza." — Génesis 1:26

blocks.en: This declaration sets humanity apart from everything else in creation. Nothing else is said to bear the image of God in this way.
blocks.es_reference: Esta declaración aparta a la humanidad de todo lo demás en la creación. Nada más se dice que lleva la imagen de Dios de esta manera.

blocks.en: At first, it may seem that this image refers primarily to intelligence. God is intelligent, so man must reflect Him in that way. Yet this explanation is insufficient. There are animals that display remarkable intelligence. Chimpanzees demonstrate exceptional short-term memory. An octopus can solve complex puzzles. Crows have been observed dropping nuts into traffic so that cars will crack them open, then waiting at crosswalks for the signal to change so they can safely retrieve their food. Intelligence alone cannot explain the image of God.
blocks.es_reference: A primera vista, podría parecer que esta imagen se refiere principalmente a la inteligencia. Dios es inteligente, así que el hombre debe reflejarlo de esa manera. Sin embargo, esta explicación es insuficiente. Hay animales que muestran inteligencia notable. Los chimpancés demuestran una memoria excepcional a corto plazo. Un pulpo puede resolver rompecabezas complejos. Se ha observado que los cuervos dejan caer nueces en el tráfico para que los autos las rompan, y luego esperan en los cruces peatonales a que cambie la señal para recuperar su comida con seguridad. La inteligencia por sí sola no puede explicar la imagen de Dios.

blocks.en: If it did, we would have to conclude that animals share in that image in the same way. Scripture makes clear that they do not. Man is set apart in a deeper and more significant way. The image of God includes rational thought, but it also includes moral awareness, the ability to discern right from wrong, the capacity for relationship, and the ability to reflect God's character.
blocks.es_reference: Si así fuera, tendríamos que concluir que los animales comparten esa imagen de la misma manera. La Escritura deja claro que no es así. El hombre está apartado de un modo más profundo y significativo. La imagen de Dios incluye el pensamiento racional, pero también incluye la conciencia moral, la capacidad de discernir el bien del mal, la capacidad de relación y la capacidad de reflejar el carácter de Dios.

blocks.en: The Image as Rational and Moral Likeness
blocks.es_reference: La Imagen como Semejanza Racional y Moral

blocks.en: Man does not simply think—he evaluates. He does not simply act—he is accountable. He does not simply exist—he relates to God. Man's greatest distinction is not merely that he can think or create, but that he can know God. No animal, regardless of intelligence, has the capacity for a personal relationship with the Creator. Man was designed not only to live in the world, but to walk with God. The image of God is most clearly seen in this capacity—to hear from God, to respond to Him, and to live in relationship with Him.
blocks.es_reference: El hombre no simplemente piensa—evalúa. No simplemente actúa—es responsable. No simplemente existe—se relaciona con Dios. La mayor distinción del hombre no es meramente que pueda pensar o crear, sino que puede conocer a Dios. Ningún animal, sin importar su inteligencia, tiene la capacidad de una relación personal con el Creador. El hombre fue diseñado no solo para vivir en el mundo, sino para caminar con Dios. La imagen de Dios se ve más claramente en esta capacidad—escuchar de Dios, responderle y vivir en relación con Él.

blocks.en: Because man bears the image of God, human life possesses inherent dignity. This dignity is not earned. It is not based on performance, success, or usefulness. It is rooted in creation itself. A person has value because he bears the image of his Creator.
blocks.es_reference: Porque el hombre lleva la imagen de Dios, la vida humana posee dignidad inherente. Esta dignidad no se gana. No se basa en el desempeño, el éxito o la utilidad. Está arraigada en la creación misma. Una persona tiene valor porque lleva la imagen de su Creador.

blocks.en: 💡 The 1,000-Peso Bill: Whether it is crisp and new or worn and lying in the gutter, its value does not change. The condition of the bill does not determine its worth. Its value rests on whose image and seal it bears. In the same way, every human being carries the image and seal of God. That image may be distorted or obscured, but it is not erased. No one is insignificant. No one is disposable. No one falls outside the boundary of dignity.
blocks.es_reference: 💡 El Billete de 1,000 Pesos: Ya sea que esté crujiente y nuevo o gastado y tirado en la cuneta, su valor no cambia. La condición del billete no determina su valor. Su valor reside en cuya imagen y sello lleva. De la misma manera, cada ser humano lleva la imagen y el sello de Dios. Esa imagen puede estar distorsionada u oscurecida, pero no está borrada. Nadie es insignificante. Nadie es desechable. Nadie está fuera del límite de la dignidad.

blocks.en: Day 3 — Human Dignity Lived Out
blocks.es_reference: Día 3 — La Dignidad Humana Vivida

blocks.en: The truth of the image of God must move beyond definition into lived reality.
blocks.es_reference: La verdad de la imagen de Dios debe moverse más allá de la definición a la realidad vivida.

blocks.en: My youngest son is, in many ways, what people often call a "spitting image" of me. When others look at him, they see a resemblance—not only in appearance, but in expression and manner. There is something in him that reflects me.
blocks.es_reference: Mi hijo menor es, en muchos aspectos, lo que la gente a menudo llama un "vivo retrato" de mí. Cuando otros lo miran, ven un parecido—no solo en apariencia, sino en expresión y manera. Hay algo en él que me refleja.

blocks.en: This helps us understand what Scripture means when it says that man is made in the image of God. We are not identical to God, nor do we possess His attributes in their fullness. Yet there is a resemblance. There is something about man that reflects his Creator. Even in a broken world, that resemblance has not disappeared.
blocks.es_reference: Esto nos ayuda a entender lo que la Escritura quiere decir cuando dice que el hombre está hecho a imagen de Dios. No somos idénticos a Dios, ni poseemos Sus atributos en su plenitud. Sin embargo, hay un parecido. Hay algo en el hombre que refleja a su Creador. Incluso en un mundo quebrantado, ese parecido no ha desaparecido.

blocks.en: Dignity Lived Out Toward Others
blocks.es_reference: La Dignidad Vivida hacia los Demás

blocks.en: This truth becomes unmistakable when it is lived out. One Thanksgiving, our family sat down to a full meal—turkey, mashed potatoes, green beans, everything prepared and served. We ate together and enjoyed the time as a family. After we finished, my oldest son quietly stood, prepared another full plate—the same meal we had just eaten—and said he would be right back. He carried the plate downstairs and out the door. We soon understood what he had done. A man was living nearby on the street in a makeshift shelter along the curb. My son took that plate of food and gave it to him. He did not offer leftovers or something less. He gave him the same meal we had received. Not long ago, he mentioned that the man is still there. Each time he passes by, he looks for an opportunity to give him something—a banana, some coins, whatever he has available.
blocks.es_reference: Esta verdad se vuelve inconfundible cuando se vive. Un Día de Acción de Gracias, nuestra familia se sentó a una comida completa—pavo, puré de papas, ejotes, todo preparado y servido. Comimos juntos y disfrutamos del tiempo en familia. Después de terminar, mi hijo mayor se paró en silencio, preparó otro plato completo—la misma comida que acabábamos de comer—y dijo que regresaría pronto. Llevó el plato abajo y salió por la puerta. Pronto entendimos lo que había hecho. Un hombre vivía cerca en la calle en un refugio improvisado junto a la acera. Mi hijo tomó ese plato de comida y se lo dio. No ofreció sobras ni algo menos. Le dio la misma comida que habíamos recibido. No hace mucho, mencionó que el hombre todavía está allí. Cada vez que pasa, busca una oportunidad para darle algo—un plátano, algunas monedas, lo que tenga disponible.

blocks.en: Why does he do this? Because that man is made in the image of God. His life may be broken. His circumstances may conceal what once reflected dignity. Yet the image remains.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Por qué hace esto? Porque ese hombre está hecho a imagen de Dios. Su vida puede estar quebrantada. Sus circunstancias pueden ocultar lo que una vez reflejó dignidad. Sin embargo, la imagen permanece.

blocks.en: The executive and the homeless man stand on equal ground. The unborn child and the elderly person share the same worth. The successful and the forgotten are equal before God. To believe in the image of God is to see people differently—and to treat them accordingly.
blocks.es_reference: El ejecutivo y el indigente están sobre terreno igual. El niño no nacido y el anciano comparten el mismo valor. El exitoso y el olvidado son iguales ante Dios. Creer en la imagen de Dios es ver a las personas de manera diferente—y tratarlas en consecuencia.

blocks.en: Day 4 — The Fall and the Distortion of Man
blocks.es_reference: Día 4 — La Caída y la Distorsión del Hombre

blocks.en: If man is created in the image of God, then the brokenness of the world demands an explanation. That explanation is found in the fall.
blocks.es_reference: Si el hombre es creado a imagen de Dios, entonces el quebrantamiento del mundo exige una explicación. Esa explicación se encuentra en la caída.

blocks.en: Genesis 3 records the moment when man rejected God's authority. This was not a minor misstep; it was rebellion. Man chose independence over dependence and self-rule over submission.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 3 registra el momento en que el hombre rechazó la autoridad de Dios. Esto no fue un pequeño error; fue rebelión. El hombre eligió la independencia sobre la dependencia y el autogobierno sobre la sumisión.

blocks.en: The consequences were immediate and far-reaching. The image of God was not destroyed, but it was profoundly distorted. The mind became darkened, the will became bent, and the desires became disordered. This condition is described as total depravity. This does not mean that man is as evil as he could possibly be. Rather, it means that every part of his being is affected by sin. There is no area that remains untouched.
blocks.es_reference: Las consecuencias fueron inmediatas y de gran alcance. La imagen de Dios no fue destruida, sino profundamente distorsionada. La mente se oscureció, la voluntad se dobló y los deseos se desordenaron. Esta condición se describe como depravación total. Esto no significa que el hombre sea tan malo como podría ser. Más bien, significa que cada parte de su ser es afectada por el pecado. No hay área que permanezca intacta.

blocks.en: The problem is not merely external—it is internal. Man does not simply commit sin; he is a sinner by nature. This is why human effort cannot solve the human problem. Education cannot remove sin. Culture cannot eliminate it. Laws cannot cure it. The issue lies within the human heart.
blocks.es_reference: El problema no es meramente externo—es interno. El hombre no simplemente comete pecado; es pecador por naturaleza. Por eso el esfuerzo humano no puede resolver el problema humano. La educación no puede eliminar el pecado. La cultura no puede erradicarlo. Las leyes no pueden curarlo. El problema yace dentro del corazón humano.

blocks.en: The fall explains why humanity is capable of both remarkable good and profound evil. It explains why man can create beauty and cause destruction—often within the same life.
blocks.es_reference: La caída explica por qué la humanidad es capaz tanto de un bien notable como de un mal profundo. Explica por qué el hombre puede crear belleza y causar destrucción—a menudo dentro de la misma vida.

blocks.en: Day 5 — Restoration in Christ
blocks.es_reference: Día 5 — Restauración en Cristo

blocks.en: The doctrine of man does not end with the fall. It leads directly to the need for redemption. What man cannot restore, God does. In Christ, the image of God is being renewed.
blocks.es_reference: La doctrina del hombre no termina con la caída. Conduce directamente a la necesidad de redención. Lo que el hombre no puede restaurar, Dios lo hace. En Cristo, la imagen de Dios se está renovando.

blocks.en: Scripture frames this restoration through two representative men. Paul calls Christ “the last Adam” (1 Corinthians 15:45): where the first Adam failed and his disobedience brought ruin to the race he represented, the last Adam obeyed perfectly, and His obedience becomes the source of renewed life for all who are in Him. So Christ succeeds precisely where the first Adam fell, undoing the distortion and restoring the image of God in His people.
blocks.es_reference: La Escritura enmarca esta restauración a través de dos hombres representativos. Pablo llama a Cristo “el postrer Adán” (1 Corintios 15:45): donde el primer Adán fracasó y su desobediencia trajo ruina a la raza que representaba, el postrer Adán obedeció perfectamente, y Su obediencia se convierte en la fuente de vida renovada para todos los que están en Él. Así que Cristo triunfa precisamente donde el primer Adán cayó, deshaciendo la distorsión y restaurando la imagen de Dios en Su pueblo.

blocks.en: Salvation is not merely forgiveness—it is transformation. Through regeneration, man is made spiritually alive. Through sanctification, the process of change begins. The Holy Spirit works within the believer to restore what sin has distorted.
blocks.es_reference: La salvación no es meramente perdón—es transformación. A través de la regeneración, el hombre es hecho espiritualmente vivo. A través de la santificación, el proceso de cambio comienza. El Espíritu Santo obra dentro del creyente para restaurar lo que el pecado ha distorsionado.

blocks.en: This restoration is both immediate and progressive. Immediately, the believer is reconciled to God. His standing is changed. Progressively, his life is transformed, and he begins to reflect more clearly the image he was created to bear.
blocks.es_reference: Esta restauración es tanto inmediata como progresiva. Inmediatamente, el creyente es reconciliado con Dios. Su posición cambia. Progresivamente, su vida se transforma y comienza a reflejar más claramente la imagen que fue creado para llevar.

blocks.en: This doctrine explains why we possess dignity, why we are broken, and why we need salvation. Salvation restores more than moral behavior—it restores relationship. What was lost in the fall was not merely innocence, but fellowship with God. What is regained in Christ is not simply forgiveness, but access. Man is brought back into the very purpose for which he was created—to know God, to walk with Him, and to live in His presence. This process continues throughout the Christian life and reaches completion when we see Christ face to face.
blocks.es_reference: Esta doctrina explica por qué poseemos dignidad, por qué estamos quebrantados y por qué necesitamos salvación. La salvación restaura más que el comportamiento moral—restaura la relación. Lo que se perdió en la caída no fue meramente la inocencia, sino la comunión con Dios. Lo que se recupera en Cristo no es simplemente el perdón, sino el acceso. El hombre es traído de vuelta al propósito mismo para el cual fue creado—conocer a Dios, caminar con Él y vivir en Su presencia. Este proceso continúa a lo largo de la vida cristiana y alcanza su consumación cuando veamos a Cristo cara a cara.

blocks.en: Final Integration
blocks.es_reference: Integración Final

blocks.en: The doctrine of man stands at the center of theology because it explains both our dignity and our need. We are not what we were created to be, yet we are not beyond restoration. In Christ, God is not abandoning His design—He is restoring it. To understand man rightly is to see both his fall and his future, and to recognize that the only true explanation of humanity is found in the God who made him.
blocks.es_reference: La doctrina del hombre está en el centro de la teología porque explica tanto nuestra dignidad como nuestra necesidad. No somos lo que fuimos creados para ser, pero no estamos más allá de la restauración. En Cristo, Dios no abandona Su diseño—lo está restaurando. Entender al hombre correctamente es ver tanto su caída como su futuro, y reconocer que la única explicación verdadera de la humanidad se encuentra en el Dios que lo hizo.

blocks.en: "For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them." — Ephesians 2:10
blocks.es_reference: "Porque somos hechura suya, creados en Cristo Jesús para buenas obras, las cuales Dios preparó de antemano para que anduviésemos en ellas." — Efesios 2:10

mc.stem: What question stands at the center of this unit?
mc.why: The unit opens by asking 'What is man?'

mc.stem: According to this unit, man is best understood as:
options: A created being understood in relation to God
mc.why: Man can only be understood in relation to the One who made him.

mc.stem: What is the foundational truth of human existence?
options: Man is created in the image of God
mc.why: Man is created in the image of God (Genesis 1:26).

mc.stem: Why does the unit reject intelligence alone as the image of God?
options: Because some animals also show notable intelligence
mc.why: Animals display intelligence, so it cannot alone explain the image of God.

mc.stem: According to this unit, man's greatest distinction is that he can:
mc.why: Man's greatest distinction is that he can know God personally.

mc.stem: Why does every human being possess inherent dignity?
options: Each person bears the image of the Creator
mc.why: Human dignity is rooted in creation, not performance.

mc.stem: What does the 1,000-peso bill illustration teach?
options: Human worth remains because of whose image is borne
mc.why: The bill's value remains because of whose image it bears; likewise, human dignity remains because of the image of God.

mc.stem: What event explains the brokenness of the world?
mc.why: The fall (Genesis 3) explains the world's brokenness.

mc.stem: What happened to the image of God in the fall?
options: It was profoundly distorted but not erased
mc.why: The image was distorted but not destroyed.

mc.stem: What does 'total depravity' mean?
options: Every person is as evil as possible
Every part of man is affected by sin
mc.why: Total depravity means every part of human nature is affected by sin.

mc.stem: In Christ, what is happening to the image of God?
mc.why: In Christ, the image of God is being renewed.

mc.stem: What was chiefly lost in the fall and restored in Christ?
mc.why: Fellowship with God was lost in the fall and restored in Christ.

mc.stem: What final truth best summarizes this unit?
options: Man is created in God's image, fallen in sin, and restored through Christ
Man is valuable only if redeemed
Man is best understood apart from theology
mc.why: Man is created, fallen, and restored through Christ.

mc.stem: What does the Thanksgiving story about the son's meal teach?
options: The homeless man bore the image of God and deserved the same meal
Leftovers are sufficient for the poor
mc.why: The son gave the same meal because the man bore the image of God.

mc.stem: According to the unit, the mind is:
mc.why: The noetic effects of sin mean the mind is darkened.

mc.stem: According to the unit, the will is:
mc.why: The will is weakened and enslaved to selfish desires.

mc.stem: According to the unit, emotions are:
mc.why: Emotions are disordered and prone to love what we should hate.

mc.stem: Sin is ultimately against:
mc.why: Every sin is first and foremost an offense against God.

mc.stem: What is the ultimate consequence of sin?
mc.why: The wages of sin is death—spiritual separation from God.

mc.stem: What does the cross show?
options: The seriousness of sin and greatness of God's love
mc.why: The cross reveals both the seriousness of sin and the depth of God's love.

sa.prompt: Explain the tension between "inherent dignity" and "total depravity." How can both be true of human beings at once?
sa.model: The unit holds two truths together that seem to pull against each other. On one side, every human being has inherent dignity because he is made in the image of God; that worth is not earned and cannot be erased. On the other side, every human being is touched by total depravity, meaning sin has reached every part of him and he cannot save himself. Both are true at once because dignity describes what man is by creation, while depravity describes what man has become by the fall. Man is a ruined masterpiece: still bearing the Maker's image and therefore precious, yet corrupted throughout and therefore in need of grace. Losing either truth distorts the doctrine of man.

sa.prompt: Explain the ontological (being) versus the functional (doing) views of the image of God. What does each emphasize?
sa.model: The unit presents two complementary ways of understanding the image of God. The ontological view focuses on being: the image consists in capacities God has given humanity that creatures lack, such as reason, moral evaluation, and the ability to relate to God. The functional view focuses on doing: the image is expressed in the role humanity carries out, representing God by ruling over and caring for creation as His stewards. One asks what man is, the other asks what man does. They are not rivals but two angles on the same truth, since man both possesses God-reflecting capacities and is called to a God-reflecting task. Together they show that to bear the image is both to be like God in certain ways and to act for God in the world.

sa.prompt: How does the doctrine of the Trinity provide a blueprint for human relationality?
sa.model: The unit teaches that because God exists as three persons in loving communion, humanity made in His image is built for relationship. The Father, Son, and Spirit have loved one another eternally, so relationality is not an add-on to God but part of who He is. When man is made in that image, it follows that he is not designed to be alone but for community and love. This is why Scripture says it is not good for man to be alone and why isolation distorts us. Human relationships at their best reflect the self-giving love within the Trinity. So the triune God serves as the blueprint: we are relational beings because we image a relational God.

sa.prompt: In what way does the Incarnation of Christ affirm the goodness of the human body?
sa.model: The unit affirms that the human person is a unity of body and soul, and the Incarnation confirms that the body is good. When the Son of God took on real human flesh and dwelt among us, He did not despise the body but assumed one, living within genuine human limits. If the body were evil or merely a prison, God would not have entered human existence in this way. The Incarnation therefore dignifies physical, embodied life and rejects the idea that the material is worthless and only the spiritual matters. Christ honored the body by taking one, and His bodily resurrection further shows that God's purpose includes the redemption of the body, not escape from it.

sa.prompt: Distinguish between the "noetic effects" of sin on the mind and a complete loss of reason. What can and cannot fallen man still do?
sa.model: The unit teaches that sin has affected every part of man, including his mind, but this does not mean reason is annihilated. The noetic effects of sin are the ways sin darkens and bends human thinking, especially toward God, so that man suppresses truth and reasons crookedly about spiritual things. Yet fallen man can still think, calculate, create, and discover real truths about the world; his reason is damaged, not deleted. The distinction matters because saying the mind is totally destroyed would deny the dignity man retains as God's image-bearer, while saying the mind is unaffected would deny the seriousness of the fall. Fallen reason is reliable in many ordinary tasks but unreliable as a path to saving knowledge of God apart from grace.

sa.prompt: Evaluate the statement: "Man is a soul that has a body." Does the unit's teaching support or correct it?
sa.model: The statement "man is a soul that has a body" needs correcting in light of the unit's teaching, because it treats the body as a mere container the real self happens to carry. Scripture presents the human person as a unity of body and soul together, not a spirit temporarily renting a body. The goodness of the body, confirmed by the Incarnation and the promise of bodily resurrection, shows that the body is part of what man is, not an accessory. A more faithful way to put it is that man is an embodied soul or a unified whole, so that what affects the body affects the person. The statement is partly right in honoring the soul, but it goes wrong if it implies the body is unimportant or detachable from true humanity.

sa.prompt: What role does "common grace" play in keeping humanity from being as evil as it could be?
sa.model: The unit teaches that although man is totally depraved, he is not as evil as he could possibly be, and the reason is common grace. Common grace is God's goodness shown to all people, believers and unbelievers alike, restraining sin and preserving a measure of order, conscience, and good in the world. It does not save anyone, but it holds back the full expression of human corruption and allows even fallen people to do relative good, build societies, and create beauty. Without it, depravity would run unchecked. So common grace explains why the world, though fallen, is not a complete hell: God actively restrains evil and grants gifts to humanity at large, even to those who do not acknowledge Him.

sa.prompt: Explain the concept of "sub-creativity" as an expression of the image of God in humanity.
sa.model: Sub-creativity, in the unit's teaching, is the human capacity to make and create that flows from being made in the image of the Creator. God is the original Maker, and because man bears His image, man also makes: building, cultivating, composing, designing, and shaping culture. We do not create out of nothing as God does; rather, we work with what He has already made, which is why our creativity is sub-creativity, under and derived from His. This capacity is one of the clearest reflections of the divine image, since it mirrors God's own creative work. When humanity creates and stewards the world well, it is fulfilling part of what it means to image God, acting as His representatives over creation.

sa.prompt: How does Christ as the "last Adam" succeed where the "first Adam" failed, and restore the image of God in His people?
sa.model: The unit frames restoration through two representative men. The first Adam failed: his disobedience brought ruin to the whole race he represented, distorting the image of God in humanity. Christ is called the last Adam, and He succeeds exactly where the first Adam fell. Where Adam disobeyed, Christ obeyed perfectly, and His obedience becomes the source of renewed life for all who are in Him. So the damage done by the first head of humanity is undone by the second: in Christ the image of God is being renewed, not merely patched. This is why the doctrine of man does not end at the fall but moves to redemption, because what was lost in Adam is recovered and restored in the last Adam.

sa.prompt: Define the teleological (purpose-driven) end for which a restored human person was created.
sa.model: The unit teaches that man was made for a purpose, and restoration in Christ brings him back to it. What was lost in the fall was not merely innocence but fellowship with God, and what is regained in Christ is not simply forgiveness but access. The teleological end of a restored person is therefore to know God, to walk with Him, and to live in His presence, reflecting His image ever more clearly. Salvation restores relationship, not just moral behavior, returning man to the very reason he was created. This purpose continues throughout the Christian life and reaches its completion when the believer sees Christ face to face. So the restored human person exists to glorify and enjoy God in unbroken fellowship.
